name: Bin Zhao

papers.title: ZeroWBC: Learning Natural Whole-Body Humanoid Interaction from Human Egocentric Data
papers.abstract: Achieving versatile and natural whole-body humanoid interaction control remains challenging due to the high cost of whole-body teleoperation data. We present ZeroWBC, a teleoperation-free framework that learns humanoid whole-body interaction from human egocentric videos paired with synchronized whole-body motion and text annotations. ZeroWBC adopts a generation-then-tracking formulation to tackle the static scene whole-body interaction control problem. Given an initial egocentric image and a language instruction, a fine-tuned Vision-Language Model generates future human whole-body motion tokens, which are decoded into continuous motions and retargeted to the humanoid. The resulting reference motions, together with root and key body-part trajectories, are then executed by a general interactive motion tracking policy. To improve interaction performance, we introduce an interaction-oriented tracking reward that prioritizes global root and key body-part trajectory alignment while preserving natural whole-body motion. Experiments on Unitree G1 humanoid robot show that ZeroWBC enables diverse scene-aware behaviors without robot teleoperation demonstrations. These results suggest a scalable paradigm for learning natural humanoid whole-body interaction from human egocentric data.
topics: 视觉语言动作与基础模型

papers.title: Learning Non-Myopic Quadrotor Pursuit in Cluttered Environments via Differentiable Physics
papers.abstract: Quadrotor pursuit-evasion in cluttered environments requires the pursuer to jointly track the evader and avoid obstacles. Policies trained with local distance or visibility rewards can become short-sighted: actions that reduce the current distance may still lead to blocked routes, unsafe maneuvers, or states with poor future capture feasibility. We propose a differentiable framework that trains non-myopic pursuit policies through closed-loop rollouts. Specifically, we introduce Global Reachability Value (GRV), a training-only value that evaluates future capture potential, guiding the policy toward obstacle-aware states that facilitate long-term success. Furthermore, to handle intermittent target observations, we introduce the Visibility-Gated Residual Belief (VGRB). This mechanism maintains target state estimation by coupling a Kalman motion prior with a visibility-gated residual predictor. In simulation validation, the proposed framework achieves 89.65%, 86.52%, and 76.04% capture rates with zero collision in three representative cluttered scenarios. Ablations show that GRV reduces myopic route-selection failures, while VGRB improves target-state estimation under occlusion. Experiments in Gazebo and real-world further validate the superiority of our framework.

papers.title: Seek-before-Act: Generative Visual Foresight for Occlusion-Aware Wrist-View Manipulation
papers.abstract:
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown substantial progress in enabling robots to act with instructions and visual observations, yet most existing policies implicitly assume that the initial observation is completely actionable. This assumption often breaks down in realistic scenes, especially wrist-view settings, where the target object may be partially visible or fully occluded.
    In such cases, manipulation failures may arise not from insufficient manipulation skill, but from the lack of a task-ready observation. To address this problem, we propose Seek-before-Act, a plug-in active approach framework that enables a robot to acquire right observations before downstream manipulation. Given only a language instruction and an initial wrist RGB image, Seek-before-Act uses task-conditioned visual foresight to imagine target-revealing view sequence, lifts them into an planning-oriented 3D representation, and plans a collision-aware approach motion toward a viewpoint that improves target visibility, reachability, and downstream manipulability. A semantic verification module further checks whether the reached view is ready for manipulation and triggers closed-loop replanning when necessary. Experiments in simulation and real-world setups show that Seek-before-Act substantially improves downstream manipulation success under occlusion, clutter, limited viewpoints, visual noise, and moderate scene changes, while remaining compatible with existing VLA policies and model-based planners.
topics: 视觉语言动作与基础模型
